s1.syndrome_frame: Acute febrile illness with flank pain and urinary symptoms
salient_findings: Urinalysis positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells
Blood and urine cultures growing Escherichia coli
key_facts: History of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
Immunosuppressive therapy with prednisone and tacrolimus
Prophylactic antimicrobial therapy with trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, itraconazole, and valganciclovir
Urinalysis positive for leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells
Blood and urine cultures growing Escherichia coli
CT of the abdomen and pelvis showing non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis and irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall

Blood and urine cultures growing Escherichia coli

shortlist.label: Pyelonephritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, flank pain, and positive urine cultures, which are consistent with pyelonephritis

shortlist.label: Urinary tract infection
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has symptoms of urinary tract infection, including dysuria and positive urinalysis

shortlist.label: Nephrolithiasis
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan shows non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis, which could be causing the patient's symptoms

shortlist.label: Bladder cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall on CT scan is suspicious for neoplasm

shortlist.label: Urosepsis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has fever, leukocytosis, and positive blood cultures, which are consistent with urosepsis

raw.rationale: The patient presents with symptoms of fever, flank pain, and foul-smelling urine, and laboratory studies show a positive urinalysis with leukocyte esterase, nitrites, and white blood cells, and both blood and urine cultures grow Escherichia coli, which are all consistent with a urinary tract infection.

rejected.label: Pyelonephritis
rejected.why: While the patient has some symptoms consistent with pyelonephritis, such as flank pain and fever, the presence of a non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis and irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall suggests a more complex urinary tract issue, but the cultures and urinalysis are more indicative of a general urinary tract infection rather than specifically pyelonephritis.

rejected.label: Nephrolithiasis
rejected.why: The patient does have a non-obstructing right nephrolithiasis, but this is not the primary cause of her current symptoms, as the cultures and urinalysis suggest an infection.

rejected.label: Bladder cancer
rejected.why: The irregular, nodular thickening of the bladder wall is suspicious for neoplasm, but the patient's current symptoms of fever, flank pain, and foul-smelling urine, along with the laboratory results, are more indicative of an infection than cancer.

rejected.label: Urosepsis
rejected.why: While the patient has a urinary tract infection with positive blood cultures, the description does not explicitly indicate sepsis, which would require evidence of a systemic inflammatory response syndrome (SIRS) with organ dysfunction, and the focus is more on the local infection symptoms and findings.
